Similar recommendations have been made for children.29 Low- molecular-weight heparins have been used; they are associated with a lower incidence of induced thrombocytopenia than unfractionated heparin30 but the rate of cross-reactivity is high and they are not generally recommended.16,25,27 Oral anticoagu- lants have also been used, but an increased risk of venous limb gangrene has been reported31 with warfarin and it should not be given until the platelet count has recovered.11,16 Dermatan sulfate32 has also been used. Thrombocytopenia has been man- aged with aspirin and dipyridamole or with normal immunoglob- ulin.33 A fibrinolytic such as urokinase has been used in a few cases of occlusive thrombosis.34,35 There may be a relationship between heparin-induced thrombo- cytopenia and skin necrosis (see below). There have been reports36 of spinal haematomas developing spontaneously after the use of low-molecular-weight heparins. 1. Walker AM, Jick H. Predictors of bleeding during heparin ther- apy.
